1.explanation: The TableBatchActions component assembles the batch actions toolbar but applies no overflow or scrolling behavior to its root container. Inside it, TableActionList simply renders a <div> with the action‐list class and likewise has no scroll styling. Because neither component enables horizontal scrolling on small screens, the toolbar’s contents are clipped. Adjustments to these two components (e.g. adding overflow-x: auto to the batch-actions wrapper or to TableActionList) are required to resolve the cutoff issue.
1.bug_scenario: On a narrow viewport (e.g. mobile) with multiple <TableBatchAction> items rendered, the blue batch‐actions bar is cut off on the left and does not scroll horizontally. The first few actions (and the cancel button) become inaccessible because neither the batch‐actions container nor the inner action‐list wrapper provides overflow or scrolling support.

2.explanation: The root of the clipping bug lives in TableBatchActions: that component renders a wrapper <div> with the batch‐action summary and then delegates all action buttons to the TableActionList container. TableActionList (via wrapComponent) emits a plain <div> with a CSS class (‘carbon--action-list’) but lacks any overflow‐scroll handling. On small screens or when many actions are present, the children simply overflow the container instead of scrolling into view. Fixing this will require adding horizontal scroll or overflow styles (or scroll controls) either in the TableActionList wrapper or by modifying the return in TableBatchActions to wrap children in a scrollable container.
2.bug_scenario: On narrow viewports (such as mobile or when many batch‐action buttons are rendered), the blue batch‐actions bar simply clips the first few <TableBatchAction> items against the left edge. The underlying <div> (TableActionList) doesn’t currently provide a horizontal scroll container, so the extra actions overflow out of view and cannot be reached.
